original_question: If sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal involution on a central simple algebra A over F, must sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to the function field F_A of the Severi-Brauer variety of A?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official target very closely. It has the right hypotheses (an anisotropic orthogonal involution σ on a central simple algebra A over a field F), the right field extension (the function field of the Severi–Brauer variety of A), and the right preservation question (whether anisotropy survives that scalar extension). In substance, it is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 7.2.
missing_details: The paper phrases this as an open problem/question ('Does σ remain anisotropic ... ?'), not as an asserted implication ('must').
If the shorthand F_A is used, it should be defined explicitly as the function field F(SB(A)) of the Severi–Brauer variety SB(A) of A.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify the scalar-extended algebra and involution: A_{F_A}=A\otimes_F F_A and σ_{F_A}=σ\otimes \mathrm{id}_{F_A}.
For full self-containment, the meaning of 'anisotropic' can be spelled out using the nearby definition from §7: σ is anisotropic if σ(x)x=0 implies x=0.

The paper places this problem in the narrower §7 context of involutions and their behavior under field extension; that contextual scope should be preserved rather than broadened to more general algebraic-group or index-reduction questions.
refined_question: Let F be a field, let A be a central simple F-algebra, and let σ be an anisotropic orthogonal involution on A. If F_A:=F(SB(A)) is the function field of the Severi–Brauer variety of A, is the scalar-extended involution σ_{F_A} on A_{F_A}=A\otimes_F F_A necessarily anisotropic; equivalently, does σ_{F_A}(x)x=0 imply x=0 for every x\in A_{F_A}?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's official Problem 7.2, and it is already very close to the printed formulation. The nearby context in §7 supplies the definition of anisotropy for orthogonal involutions, frames Problem 7.2 as a Severi–Brauer-function-field variant of the odd-degree-extension question in Problem 7.1, and explains that a positive answer to Problem 7.2 would imply the orthogonal case of Problem 7.1 by Springer's theorem; it also notes a converse in index 2. Since your draft already captures the official problem, the refinement only makes the notation F_A explicit, spells out scalar extension, and adds the anisotropy condition so the question is fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
